findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE value changed from 4 to 3, repurposing exit code 4
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was previously 4 and is now changed to 3, with the freed-up value 4 reassigned to the new FEATURE_DISABLED constant. The update-compatibility check/metadata commands already existed before this PR (only +4/+7 line diffs were needed to add the feature-flag gating), meaning this exit code contract was already shipped and could be relied upon by external automation/scripts that branch on exit code 4 meaning 'recreate update required'. After this change, the same scripts will now interpret exit code 4 as 'feature disabled' and exit code 3 as 'recreate required', silently breaking any existing integration built against the previous exit code semantics. This renumbering is not mentioned in the PR description and should be called out as a breaking change (or avoided by picking an unused code for FEATURE_DISABLED).

findings.title: No test for operator failing when update.strategy is set without the rolling-updates feature enabled
findings.body: The updated docs (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc) explicitly state: 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Operator will fail.' However, createInitialDeployment() in this test only ever enables the ROLLING_UPDATES feature together with a non-null UpdateStrategy, and only exercises the default (updateStrategy == null, feature not enabled) and explicit-strategy-with-feature-enabled combinations. There is no test exercising the documented failure path where an explicit update.strategy is configured in the Keycloak CR while the rolling-updates feature is left disabled, so the documented 'Operator will fail' behavior is never verified by this test suite.

findings.title: CAUTION about rolling-updates feature requirement is overly broad relative to actual default behavior
findings.body: The new CAUTION block states unconditionally that 'the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail', placed directly under the 'Managing Keycloak Operator Updates' heading before any mention of the optional update.strategy field. This reads as if the feature flag is required any time this section's functionality (including the default/unconfigured behavior) is used. But per the accompanying UpgradeTest.java changes, when updateStrategy is left unset (no 'update' stanza in the CR), the Operator falls back to legacy (pre-rolling-updates) behavior without requiring the feature flag at all. The caution should clarify that the feature is only required when explicitly setting the `update.strategy` field, not for all uses of the Operator's update handling, to avoid confusing users into thinking the flag is always mandatory.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the printed error message ('Unable to use this command. The preview feature ...') but never asserts that the process exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), which is the new behavior introduced by this PR. Since this PR also changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces FEATURE_DISABLED as 4, the actual exit code values are an important, easily-regressed part of the contract and should be explicitly verified by this test (and by the recreate-path tests) rather than relying solely on message text.
